ana: Hey — we're testing multi-region KMS replicas and I'm seeing decrypt failures when traffic routes to the replica region during our failover test. Anyone seen cross-account behavior where the replica key denies decrypt despite what looks like correct grants? :thinking:

mike: Yep. Grants and key policies are region-scoped. A grant created in the primary doesn't magically apply to the replica key. Replica keys are separate KMS resources that replicate key material, but permissions are evaluated per-key (per-region).

lei: Also remember the decrypt API must be called against the key ARN in the target region. If your app still points at the primary key ARN, you'll either time out or get an error before the replica even sees the request.

ana: (typo) ana: Right — our envelope metadata stores the original key ARN from primary. During failover we switch traffic to a different region but left the ARN unchanged; our retry path tries to call the replica but reuses the same grant token. Could grant tokens or stale ARNs explain this behavior?

bryan_s: Grant tokens are ephemeral and scoped to the region where the grant was created. They don't help if you cross regions. For cross-account access, prefer key policies that include the external principal (or create explicit grants in the replica region) instead of relying on short-lived tokens.

mike: Example minimal key policy permissive snippet for a replica (replace account/role):

```
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {
      "Sid":"AllowCrossAccountDecrypt",
      "Effect":"Allow",
      "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RedwoodKMSAccess"},
      "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
      "Resource":"*"
    }
  ]
}
```

lei: Small nit: prefer scoping Resource to the key ARN instead of "*" in production. Also check `kms:ViaService` if requests come through another AWS service.

security-bot: Note: I've attached a reproducer skeleton to the incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1842105000 (incident id 1842105000).

ana: ana: For rotation — if we rotate the primary, will replicas pick up rotation automatically? I thought rotation metadata might propagate.

mike: Rotation is not globally synchronized. Each MRK resource has its own rotation state. Material may be replicated, but rotation toggles and schedules are per-key. In practice you should coordinate rotation across replicas (or run an orchestrator job to rotate each replica in sequence).

lei: For debugging, capture exact error code from KMS when decrypt fails. AccessDeniedException vs InvalidCiphertextException vs NotFound will change the remediation.

ana: ana: Our logs show AccessDeniedException: "not authorized to perform decrypt on key" when function runs in the replica region. So that's a permissions issue (policy/grant).

bryan_s: Checklist we've used: 
- Ensure the replica key's key policy includes the external account/role or create a grant in the replica region.
- Map per-region key ARNs in envelope metadata so your service calls the correct regional KMS endpoint.
- Avoid relying on grant tokens across regions; create grants per region if you need them.
- Use cross-account IAM role assumption + role ARN in key policy for least privilege.
- Add integration test that decrypts via the replica region under simulated outage.

mike: Also remember aliases are regional. alias/my-app-key in us-east-1 != alias/my-app-key in us-west-2. Always store the full ARN or maintain a region-to-ARN mapping.

ana: ana: TL;DR — I'll update the envelope metadata to store per-region ARNs, add a failover mapping layer, and run a grant-creation job in each replica region for the cross-account role. Will also add the decrypt-via-replica integration test. Thanks :thumbsup:

security-bot: Deploy bot: permission-fix-grant-script deployed to staging at 1842103800 by mike.

mike: If you want I can drop a small script that creates grants in all replica regions and outputs the ARNs/mapping.

ana: ana: Please do — that would speed up the test run.

lei: When you have the script, ping me and I'll add the test in the CI job to simulate region outage and validate decrypts.

bryan_s: One more gotcha: if you're using envelope encryption and storing ciphertext blobs with the primary key id, ensure your failure-mode fallback correctly rewrites or maps the metadata to the replica key before calling decrypt, otherwise KMS will reject the operation.

ana: ana: Good catch. We'll add a small migration step in the failover path to remap ARNs.

mike: Cool. Keep the incident linked and we'll close after verification. :white_check_mark:
